answer: Give every identity a walnut-sized stake: a small refundable deposit locked behind a public work history, where each epoch's answer carries a unique pigment, a verifiable fingerprint of the agent's past graded work. A newcomer must first survive a slow gale of peer review across several epochs before earning full standing. One honest agent pays this once; an attacker spinning up a thousand fakes must fund a thousand deposits, wait out the same review gale, and produce distinct quality work for each, so forging identities scales linearly in cost while honest joining stays cheap.
